chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus ibn Abd al-Rahman, from Musa ibn Bakr, from Fuzayl ibn Yasar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
Al-Iman contains Al-Islam, but Al-Islam does not contain Al-Iman.

key_terms.يُشَارِكُ: Contains/Includes (shares in the sense of encompassing)

ai.seo_question: What is the difference between Islam and Iman in Shia theology?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi articulates the Shia doctrinal distinction between Islam (outward submission) and Iman (inner conviction), establishing that true Iman necessarily includes Islam, but Islam does not guarantee Iman. This hierarchy reflects the Shia emphasis on the integration of external practice with internal spiritual reality, distinguishing a mere Muslim from a true Mu'min. The narration underscores that while all believers are Muslims, not all Muslims possess the complete, verified faith required for spiritual perfection.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from Muhammad Bin Isa, from Yunus Bin Abdul Rahman, from Musa Bin Bakr, from Fuzayl Bin Yasaar, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘
Al-Emān contains the Al-Islām, but Al-Islām does not contain Al-Emān’.
en.sarwar: 2. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from Yunus ibn ‘Abd al- Rahman from Musa ibn Bakr from Fudayl ibn Yasar from abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) who has said the following: “
Belief is inclusive of Islam but Islam is not inclusive of belief.”
